plan: First playable: Linky hops between clouds and one tap picks one of two or three answer gates for addition and subtraction within 20, over 10 gentle stages; a wrong gate just loops back. Scores and speed-up are left out.
First playable: 15 stages where the friend hops along a number line of stones by tapping jump sizes to reach a target, first 0 to 10 then crossing zero into negatives. Free-form equations come later.

First playable: 12 garden beds where flowers are planted in rows and columns to make a requested area, showing the matching multiplication fact and skip counting. Division and timed tables are left out.
First playable: 20 toy-train patterns from AB to ABC and growing patterns where one of three big carriages is chosen or dragged into the gap, with a choo-choo reward. Number sequences come later.
First playable: picture 4x4 and number 6x6 Sudoku generated with unique solutions, 10 tutorial grids, notes, undo and a next-step hint. 9x9 and variant rules come later.

First playable: no-guess treasure fields from 5x5 to 9x9 where clue envelopes count adjacent treasure, with flagging, undo and a solver hint; mistakes reveal a friendly mole instead of losing. Probability mode comes later.

First playable: 20 kitchen orders where a pie or vegetable is cut into equal shares with guided slices and the shares are served to plates, from halves to eighths. Fraction addition and number notation come later.

First playable: 30 balance puzzles where tokens are added or removed from both pans of a scale until one mystery box stands alone, slowly turning into letters and numbers. Fractions and parentheses are deferred.
First playable: generated small Kakuro grids from 3x3 to 6x6 with sum clues, a factor-pair helper panel and 12 tutorial grids. Large grids and multiplication cages are left out.
First playable: three pegs with 2 to 7 acorn disks, a gentle refusal for illegal moves, a move counter compared with the minimum and an optional recursion replay. Four-peg variants are left out.
First playable: 20 bead strings of 3 to 8 switches toggled to reach a target number, with a running place-value total under each bead. Binary addition and hexadecimal are left for later.

First playable: cards drawn from shape, colour, count and pattern; early rounds pick one of three cards sharing an attribute, later rounds find full sets in a deal of nine. Competitive speed play is left out.
First playable: 20 authored 3x3 and 4x4 logic grids with illustrated friends and voiced picture clues, cross and tick marks and a contradiction-explaining hint. Generated puzzles come later.

First playable: 12 experiments with an editable spinner and two dice where the child predicts, spins 1 to 100 times and watches a bar chart approach the expected shape. Betting and conditional probability are left out.

First playable: a compass and straightedge geometry kernel with snapping intersections and 20 goal-checked constructions, from perpendicular bisectors to a hexagon. Proof writing and free play are left out.

First playable: 20 delivery maps where routes are drawn between flower junctions on weighted paths, compared with the shortest route and replayed step by step as Dijkstra search. Travelling-salesman rounds come later.

First playable: 30 proof puzzles where a Links Notation expression is rewritten by dragging one of a few visible inference rules onto it until the goal appears, with a proof tree and hints. Free proving is left out.
First playable: generated Hashi boards from 5x5 to 9x9 where taps place one or two bridges, with connectivity checking, 10 tutorial boards and a next-bridge hint. Daily boards are left out.
First playable: generated Futoshiki gardens from 4x4 to 6x6 with clear greater-than gates, notes, undo and 10 tutorial boards. Larger boards and killer variants are left out.

First playable: 100 solvable hands of four number cards dragged with operation tiles into an expression tree that evaluates live, with a solver hint for stuck hands. Fractions and target numbers other than 24 come later.
